manifest.name: Studio Docs
manifest.description: Studio host (studio.*) tool catalog + concepts. Knowledge-only bundle — no UI, no agents. Auto-loaded as seed at host boot, knowledge.sources fanned out as studio://knowledge/<src>/<doc> MCP resources.

agents.name: Studio Manager
agents.systemPrompt:
You are the AppPlayer Studio manager. Your sole job is to coordinate host inventory and delegate to specialist agents.

The "Available tools" section below your prompt lists the EXACT tools you have access to in this session. They are real and callable — invoke them directly to answer the user. Do not greet the user, do not echo the routing rules, do not ask for clarification on straightforward queries. Do the work.

Built-in domains:
  • app_builder   — author mcp_ui_dsl bundles (`app_builder.*` / `studio.builder.*`).
  • scene_builder — record demo / tutorial scenarios (`studio.recorder.*` / `studio.scenario.*`).
  • makemind_ops  — workspace operations (`makemind_ops.*`).

Routing:
  • Agent listing / id query → call `bk.agent.list` immediately and return the result.
  • Agent metadata / single record → call `bk.agent.get`.
  • Dispatch to a specialist agent → call `bk.agent.dispatch` with the target agent id.
  • Bundle listing / install query → call the matching `host.*` / `<bundle>.*` tool from the catalog.
  • Knowledge / fact query → call `bk.knowledge.query` / `bk.fact.query`.
  • Ambiguous intent (only when truly ambiguous) → ask one short clarification question.

Never guess identifiers — call the relevant `*.list` tool first when you need them. Answer in the user's language.

sources.title: Studio host tools (studio.*) catalog
sources.description: Always-registered studio.* MCP tools — host-side surface every domain shares. Source = docs/06_OPS/reference/studio-tool-catalog.md.

documents.title: Overview — host vs domain surface
documents.content: Studio host registers studio.* tools at boot. They are available regardless of which domain is active. Domains (App Builder · Scene Builder · …) layer their own tools on top via BuiltInApp.registerHostTools. The mcp connection at system URL (default :7831) multiplexes all domains. Per-domain narrow links (inheritFromSystem=false) get studio.* mirror + single domain only (see MOD-INFRA-010).

documents.title: host capability packs — io · channel · browser · fs · db · canvas · kv · analysis · form · ingest · secret
documents.content:
Beyond `studio.*`, the host registers reusable **capability tool packs** (`<id>.*`) — shared by every domain and bundle app, not per-domain. Logic lives in the `mcp_*` packages / the `capability_tools` recipe; the host only wires adapters + policy (built-in = UI + wiring). Design: `docs/03_DDD/capability-tools.md`.

- **io.\*** (sandboxed OS exec — exe allowlist git/dart/flutter/pub · allowedRoots jail · manager/operator roles): `io.execute` (policy-gated) · `io.plan_execute`→`io.commit_execute` (dangerous → dry-run → commit) · `io.read` · `io.subscribe` · `io.list_devices`/`describe_device`/`connect_device`/`disconnect_device` · `io.list_jobs`/`get_job`/`cancel_job`/`emergency_stop`. Process steps run dev commands (git/dart/flutter/pub) through `io.execute`.
- **channel.\*** (bidirectional messaging — in-app feed + connectors): `channel.send` · `channel.receive` · `channel.list` · `channel.status` · `channel.session.history`. Handoffs / notify route here.
- **browser.\*** (shared headless browser): `page_view` · `page_audit_role` · `web_search` · `extract` · `crawl` · `monitor` · `submit_form` · `download` · `open_login` · `auth_capture` · `page_compare_actors`.
- **fs.\*** (datastore filesystem — jailed to the config root): `read` · `write` · `edit` · `list` · `glob` · `stat` · `mkdir` · `move` · `remove` (destructive → needs an explicit commit).
- **db.\*** (sqlite datastore): `query` · `exec` · `tx`.
- **canvas.\*** (CDL 2D/3D engine): `cdl_to_json` · `json_to_cdl` · `validate_cdl`.
- **kv.\*** (key/value store): `set` · `get` · `exists` · `keys` · `remove`.
- **analysis.\*** (spec-driven analysis): `run` · `list_specs` · `get_job`.
- **form.\*** (template/binding + 5 renderers): `create_document` · `render` · `patch` · `validate` · `export` · `list_templates` · `get_status`.
- **ingest.\*** (document chunking → facts): `ingest.run`.
- **secret.\*** (credential vault over the OS keychain — `appplayer_secure`, namespace `appplayer.credentials`): `set` · `exists` · `remove` · `list` (keys only). **No plaintext `get`** — a secret is resolved internally only when a capability needs it (e.g. an authenticated HTTP GET), never returned. An asset (`category:"asset"` fact) holds only a `credentialRef`; the secret body lives here. Wired via `registerSecretVault` (vendored `secure_capability` recipe). Migration = `credentials_export`/`import` (Ops) over the passphrase `CredentialMigrator`.


All host-shared: every workspace/agent reaches them via `<id>.*` (no per-domain registration). Datastore writes are role-gated (manager/operator); destructive ops (`fs.remove`) require commit. NOTE: `fs.*` here is the **datastore** capability, distinct from `studio.fs.*` (workspace file tools).

Usage patterns (per capability) = `studio://knowledge/studio_capability_recipes/*`.

documents.title: studio.agent.* — agent runtime
documents.content: studio.agent.list / describe / dispatch / history / clear_history / set_model. Manages registered LLM agents (manifest.agents[] entries from active bundles). dispatch sends one turn to a specific agent and returns text + tool_use blocks. set_model swaps model id at runtime.

documents.title: studio.builder.* — bundle mutator (Studio domain)
documents.content: Atomic mutators for the active Studio domain bundle (NOT App bundles). readManifest / readBundle / writeUI / patchManifest / addAgent / addTool / addSkill / addProfile / addPhilosophy / addSlashCommand / addDomainAction / addKnowledge* / addSettings* / writeScenario / ui.{addNode, setProp, moveNode, removeNode, reorderChildren, applyPatch, findNodes, readNode, readTree, diff, catalog.list, catalog.schema, catalog.diag} / lib.{create, delete, list, placeAsTemplate, placeInline, read, rename, render}. App bundles use App Builder's vibe_* tools (or app_builder.<family>.<verb> aliases) instead — see app_builder seed docs.

documents.title: studio.bundle.* — package lifecycle + resources
documents.content: install / uninstall / activate / list / list_files / read_file / list_assets / read_asset / dispatch_tool. install accepts .mcpb archive or .mbd/ dir, registers in bundle pool. activate makes a tab. list returns installed bundles. read_file/read_asset for arbitrary file access within bundle root. dispatch_tool invokes a bundle-declared tool.

documents.title: studio.chrome.* — shell wiring
documents.content: list_tabs / select_tab / close_tab / reload_tab / create_package / open_{settings, history, agents, onboarding, seed} / peek_tab_bar / set_tab_bar / toggle_left_panel / set_left_panel. Drives tab strip, left panel, header dialogs. select_tab takes key (path or 'home').

documents.title: studio.project.* — active bundle's project lifecycle
documents.content: info / close / new / open / recents / create / export. Operates on the CURRENT TAB's project context — App Builder's currentProject, Scene Builder's scene project, etc. project.new scaffolds via the active bundle's newProjectInActive bridge slot. project.info returns {packageName, packagePath, projectPath, projectName} or {} on home tab.

documents.title: studio.fs.* — workspace-gated file IO
documents.content: list / read / write / mkdir / delete / glob. Bounded to workspaceDir — paths outside throw. Use for project-bound file access. App bundle authoring should prefer vibe_file_* via active App Builder (project-root scoped) — studio.fs.* is broader workspace scope. Per-workspace content/assets (the bound project's `knowledge/`) go through `knowledge_file_*` / `knowledge_fact_save`, not the config-jailed `fs.*` (which writes under the host config root, not the workspace). `glob({pattern, path?, limit?})` walks recursive matching `**`/`*` (e.g. `**/manifest.json`, `ui/**/*.json`); returns `{count, matches:[absPath], truncated?}` capped at limit (default 500).

documents.title: studio.knowledge.* — RAG over registered knowledge sources
documents.content: query / test / validate. query({text, limit?}) returns top-N hits across all registered sources (seed bundles' knowledge.sources fanned out as resources). test validates query interpretation. validate runs lint on the active bundle's knowledge entries.

documents.title: studio.ui.* — UI control
documents.content: Full pointer + keyboard + focus + dropdown automation via Flutter binding (no macOS accessibility). · `studio.ui.set_center_mode` (UI/Bundle/Debug 3-way switch). · `studio.ui.tap` ({elementId or x+y, mode?:tap|long|double}) — synthetic click; elementId resolves via layout-snapshot rect resolver (accepts bare `id` OR `<type>:<key>`). · `studio.ui.type` ({text, elementId?, clear?, submit?}) — focused TextField TextEditingController direct set (bypasses IME / Korean+CJK garble); submit:true fires onSubmitted (Enter). · `studio.ui.dismiss_dialog` — pop topmost route on root Navigator. · `studio.ui.scroll` ({elementId or x+y, dx, dy}) — wheel scroll. · `studio.ui.hover` — pointer hover only (no click) for tooltip/hover decoration capture. · `studio.ui.right_click` — secondary-button tap (onSecondaryTap / context menu). · `studio.ui.drag` ({from, to, steps?}) — splitter / drag-and-drop / canvas pan. · `studio.ui.focus` — first EditableText.focusNode.requestFocus() without tap. · `studio.ui.element_value` — read EditableText `{value, hasFocus, selection}` (inverse of `type`). · `studio.ui.key` ({key:enter|escape|tab|arrow*|backspace|space, char?, modifiers:[shift|ctrl|alt|meta]}) — macOS keyevent platform channel. · `studio.ui.popover_entries` — enumerate active PopupMenu/Dropdown items as `[{value, label, enabled, rect}]`.

documents.title: studio.debug.* — diagnostic surface (~24 tools)
documents.content: studio.debug.* — 28 tools. boot/notify/dispatch_log · activation/bundles/tabs/chrome/runtimes/runtime_state/agents/chat/header_actions · config/settings/overrides · screenshot/layout_snapshot/snapshot_diff · servers (DomainServerManager pool) · history.{list,diff,restore} · dispatch_tool · set_state · wait_for · workspace_snapshot. NEW (2026-05-20): debug.overrides ({path?}) reads package_settings/*.json per-domain inherit/url overrides · debug.workspace_snapshot lists workspaceDir mbds+projects+other entries.

documents.title: studio.renderer.* — domain UI activation
documents.content: activate / current_view / layout_snapshot / screenshot / screenshot_region / image_diff. Drives the active domain UI mount. `layout_snapshot` walks chrome captureRoot AND adds `WidgetsBinding.rootElement` walk so showDialog overlays surface too. `image_diff` ({a, b base64 PNGs, threshold?}) returns `{score, diffPixels, totalPixels, w, h}` for visual regression — both inputs must share dimensions.

documents.title: studio.overlay.* — in-frame markup
documents.content: push / list / remove / clear. Annotation/highlight markers on top of the renderer. Used by Scene Builder for scenario overlays.

documents.title: studio.recorder.* — frame capture + encoding
documents.content: start / stop / status / recordings.list / encode / mark / caption. Captures frames at fps, encodes to mp4. `status` returns `markers[]` + `captions[]` (timeline `{label or text, startMs/elapsedMs, durationMs}`). `mark({label})` drops a chapter marker, `caption({text, durationMs?})` logs a subtitle (pair with `studio.overlay.push` for burn-in). Used by Scene Builder for scenario recordings + tutorial videos.

documents.title: studio.scenario.* — scenario list/run/save
documents.content: list / read / preview / run / save. Scene Builder's scenario format. preview = dry-run, run = with side effects.

documents.title: studio.scene.project.* — Scene Builder project lifecycle
documents.content: info / new / open. Sibling to studio.project.* but scene-specific (different storage layout).

documents.title: studio.chat.send — chat composer programmatic input
documents.content: Send a chat turn through the active tab's composer. Same path as user typing in chat panel.

documents.title: studio.{settings, search, workspace, meta}
documents.content: settings.get({key, path?}) - read system or domain override (per-package). settings.set({key, value, path?}) - write system OR per-domain override; **domain set triggers DomainServerManager.detach+attach automatically (runtime re-attach, no restart needed)**. System settings include `themeMode` (system/light/dark) and `debugMode` (boolean). When `debugMode=true`, every DslWorkspaceView mounts its bundle through `MCPUIRuntime.withInspector(widgetWrapper:)` so every rendered widget is tagged with MetaData — required for `studio.renderer.layout_snapshot` to surface inner-bundle widgets and for `studio.ui.tap({elementId:...})` to address them by name. Off by default (production fast path); flip true for scripted UI tests / tutorial recordings / external-LLM debugging. Toggle is live (no restart) — DslWorkspaceView listens on `ChromeBridge.inspectorEnabled` and re-mounts when it flips. search.query - workspace-wide text search. workspace.adopt - bring external folder into workspace mode. meta.list_tools / describe_tool - runtime tool discovery.

sources.title: Host capability recipes — io · datastore · canvas · kv · analysis · channel · ingest · form
sources.description: Usage patterns (not just the verb list) for the shared host capability packs. Pairs with the studio_host_tools `capabilities` catalog. Agents drive real work — commands, files, db, rendering, messaging — through these.

documents.title: io.* — sandboxed OS execution
documents.content:
# io.* — sandboxed OS execution

Run dev commands only (`git` · `dart` · `flutter` · `pub`) under policy: exe allowlist, `allowedRoots` jail (config root), manager/operator roles, no shell.

| do | call |
|---|---|
| safe command | `io.execute({exe:'git', argv:['status']})` → `{exitCode, stdout, stderr}` |
| dangerous (push/publish) | `io.plan_execute` (dry-run + risk) → `io.commit_execute` (after sign-off) |
| long job | `io.get_job` · `io.cancel_job` · `io.emergency_stop` |

Read-only subcommands (analyze/test/version/status/log/diff/get) run unattended; mutating ones gate on the process's approval step. Pattern — a process step does real work:
```
step: { skillId: io.execute, inputs: { exe: dart, argv: [analyze] } }
```

documents.title: fs.* / db.* — datastore (filesystem + sqlite)
documents.content:
# fs.* / db.* — datastore (filesystem + sqlite)

`fs.*` is jailed to the config root (a path escaping it is rejected). `db.*` is a sqlite source. Distinct from `studio.fs.*` (workspace files).

| do | call |
|---|---|
| read / write a file | `fs.read({path})` · `fs.write({path, text})` |
| edit in place | `fs.edit({path, oldString, newString})` |
| list / find | `fs.list({path})` · `fs.glob({pattern})` |
| delete (destructive) | `fs.remove({path})` → `needs_commit`; requires explicit plan→commit |
| read query | `db.query({statement, params})` → `{rows}` |
| mutate | `db.exec({statement, params})` → `{affected}` |
| atomic batch | `db.tx({statements:[{statement, params}]})` |

Writes are role-gated (manager/operator); destructive `fs.remove` needs commit. Pattern — a process step writes a report (`fs.write`); an agent persists state (`db.exec`/`db.query`).

documents.title: canvas.* — CDL 2D/3D
documents.content:
# canvas.* — CDL 2D/3D

Author / validate Canvas Description Language. A CDL document begins with `type "name" { ... }`.

| do | call |
|---|---|
| CDL → JSON | `canvas.cdl_to_json({cdl})` |
| JSON → CDL | `canvas.json_to_cdl({json})` |
| validate first | `canvas.validate_cdl({cdl})` → `{ok, error?}` |

Pure value engine (no side effects). Always `validate_cdl` before rendering or persisting.

documents.title: kv.* — key/value store
documents.content:
# kv.* — key/value store

Small workspace-scoped JSON state (for bulk/relational data use `db.*`).
`kv.set({key, value})` · `kv.get({key})` · `kv.exists({key})` · `kv.keys({prefix?})` · `kv.remove({key})`.

Pattern — a skill stashes a cursor / checkpoint between runs.

documents.title: analysis.* — spec-driven analysis
documents.content:
# analysis.* — spec-driven analysis

`analysis.list_specs({search?})` → pick a spec id → `analysis.run({specId, params})` → `{jobId}` → `analysis.get_job({jobId})` for status/result.

Long jobs are async — poll `get_job`.

documents.title: channel.* — messaging
documents.content:
# channel.* — messaging

`channel.send({channelId, conversationId, text})` — `channelId:'in_app'` = internal feed (reversible, auto-allowed); external connectors gate as destructive. `channel.receive` injects an inbound message (agentic loop). `channel.list` · `channel.status` · `channel.session.history` for state.

Pattern — a process handoff posts to an in-app thread (a step's `channelThreadId`); notify a person via `channel_notify`.

documents.title: ingest.* — document chunking → facts
documents.content:
# ingest.* — document chunking → facts

`ingest.run({...})` chunks a document into retrievable pieces that feed the knowledge fact graph. In Ops, `knowledge_ingest_file` wraps this capability.

documents.title: form.* — document generation
documents.content:
# form.* — document generation

`form.list_templates` → `form.create_document({templateId, data})` → `form.render` → `form.export`. Validate with `form.validate`. Template-driven reports / documents (5 renderers).

documents.title: secret.* — credential vault + cross-machine migration
documents.content:
# secret.* — credential vault + cross-machine migration

Keyed credential store over the OS keychain (`appplayer_secure`). An operational **asset** (`category:"asset"` knowledge fact with metadata `kind` / `location` / `locator` / `capability` / `credentialRef`) keeps only the `credentialRef`; the secret body lives in the vault.

| do | call |
|---|---|
| store a secret | `secret.set({ref, value})` |
| check / list refs | `secret.exists({ref})` · `secret.list({prefix?})` (keys only) |
| remove | `secret.remove({ref})` |

**No plaintext `get`** (vault discipline) — the secret is resolved internally when a capability operates the asset (Ops `asset_open` → `db.query` / `browser.page_view` / authenticated HTTP `Authorization: Bearer`).

**Cross-machine migration** — Ops `credentials_export({passphrase})` seals the workspace's asset credentials under a passphrase (PBKDF2 → AEAD; the keychain key never leaves the device) into a portable blob; `credentials_import({passphrase, sealed})` restores them on another machine. `.opspack` export/import carry the sealed blob when `includeSecrets:true`. Core = the recipe's `CredentialMigrator`; deciding which refs to migrate (collecting `credentialRef`s from asset facts) is the host's job. Canon: `specs/platform/14-asset-credentials.md`.

sources.title: Studio host concepts
sources.description: Architectural concepts external LLM should know.

documents.title: Host vs Domain — superset / subset
documents.content: Studio = AppPlayer superset. AppPlayer base = renderer + atom + MCP dispatch + standard wiring. Studio adds: studio.builder.* mutators + chrome lifecycle slot fire + integrated builder UI surface (3-way switch) + studio Vbu* atoms (chrome/inspector). Bundles declare capability via manifest.requires.builtinAtoms / builtinTools — Studio fills more than AppPlayer.

documents.title: Tab vs Install — workspace project vs installed bundle
documents.content: App Builder's currentProject (under workspace/) is NOT an installed bundle — it sits in the App Builder built-in tab as the project being authored. Once packed (vibe_build_pack_bundle → .mcpb) and installed (studio.bundle.install), it gains a SEPARATE tab and appears in Home's INSTALLED APPS section. Tabs.json persists open tabs across sessions including installed ones.

documents.title: Domain MCP server inheritance — system vs per-domain
documents.content: Each domain has inheritFromSystem (default true). ON = share the system MCP server at default URL. OFF = DomainServerManager.spawn allocates a separate URL/port for narrow connection. Per MOD-INFRA-010, the per-domain server mirrors host studio.* tools + that domain's tools + knowledge. Reduces noise for external clients that work with one domain at a time.

documents.title: Tool name aliases — flat vs categorized
documents.content: App Builder's inner vibe_* tools are exposed on host with BOTH names: original vibe_<family>_<verb> AND categorized alias app_builder.<family>.<verb>. Same handler. Use either — categorized version is easier to scan in tools/list.

documents.title: Knowledge separation — host vs domain
documents.content: Studio host (studio.* tool catalog · architecture concepts) lives in seed studio_docs.mbd's knowledge.sources. Each domain's tool catalog lives in that domain's seed bundle (app_builder.mbd, scene_builder.mbd). resources/list shows the union. studio.knowledge.query searches across all. Cross-domain answers blend host + multiple domain docs.

sources.name: Built-in apps catalog
sources.description: The four built-in apps the host ships - id / label / purpose / tool surface / default agent. Manager reads this to route bundle requests.

documents.title: app_builder · App Builder
documents.content:
Built-in id: app_builder
Label: App Builder
Default chat agent: app_builder.manager (declared in seed manifest by `role: manager`).
Purpose: author mcp_ui_dsl bundles. The user describes an app in chat; the manager dispatches to specialists (`ux_designer` → wireframes · `tool_designer` → tool catalogs · `knowledge_designer` → knowledge sources · `ui_implementer` → mcp_ui_dsl JSON via `studio.builder.*` mutators · `dart_converter` / `embed_converter` → export to .app or LVGL/Qt · `debug_analyst` → diagnose).
Tool surface (high level): `studio.project.*` (new/open/save) · `studio.builder.*` (44 mutators) · `studio.knowledge.query` · `studio.chrome.reload_tab` · `studio.renderer.screenshot` · `newAppProject` · `convertToDart` · `convertToEmbed`.
Knowledge sources (consult before authoring): `app_builder_six_layers` (8 docs) · `app_builder_wiring` · `app_builder_pitfalls` · `dart_conversion_patterns` · `embed_conversion_patterns` · `mcp_ui_dsl_widgets` · `mcp_ui_dsl_state_actions` · `mcp_ui_dsl_custom_widgets` · `bundle_structure` · `chat_surface` · `ux_patterns` · `ops_patterns` · `knowledge_design_patterns` · `common_pitfalls` · `external_llm_app_builder`.
Trigger from Home: user says 'new app' / 'edit bundle' / 'export to dart' → host manager invokes `bk.agent.dispatch` with target `app_builder.manager` after ensuring the App Builder tab is open (`studio.chrome.*`).

documents.title: scene_builder · Scene Builder
documents.content:
Built-in id: scene_builder
Label: Scene Builder
Default chat agent: scene_builder.manager.
Purpose: author tutorial / demo / scenario videos as scripted MCP-tool sequences. The user describes a click-through; the manager records each step with overlay + caption + screen capture and emits an MP4.
Tool surface: `studio.scenario.*` (5 — list / save / read / run / preview) · `studio.recorder.*` (7 — start / stop / status / caption / mark / encode / recordings.list) · `studio.overlay.*` (4 — push / list / remove / clear) · `studio.scene.project.*` (3 — new / open / info) · `studio.ui.*` (tap / drag / hover) · `studio.renderer.*` (activate / current_view / layout_snapshot / screenshot).
Knowledge: `scene_builder_tool_surface` (5 docs).
Trigger from Home: user says 'record a demo' / 'capture this flow' / 'make a tutorial video' → host manager opens the Scene Builder tab and dispatches to `scene_builder.manager`.

documents.title: makemind_ops · Ops
documents.content:
Built-in id: makemind_ops
Label: Ops
Default chat agent: ops.manager.
Purpose: workspace operations — members / tasks / processes / philosophies / skills / agents / knowledge / bundles. A project-bound surface (per-project root); each project lives at `<workspaceDir>/<project>/` with marker `project.opsproj` + per-workspace `.mbd` directories.
Tool surface: `makemind_ops.*` family — workspace_create / workspace_list / member_* / task_* / process_* / skill_* / profile_* / philosophy_* / knowledge_* / bundle_* + 9 browser primitives (page_view / web_search / extract / crawl / monitor / submit_form / download / page_audit_role / page_compare_actors). Plus the kernel-standard `bk.*` surface.
Knowledge: `ops_overview` (5 docs — overview · capabilities · workspace_structure · tool_surface · agents).
Trigger from Home: user says 'manage workspace' / 'add member' / 'kick off process' → host manager opens the Ops tab and dispatches to `ops.manager`.

documents.title: Form Builder
documents.content:
Built-in id: form_builder
Label: Form Builder
Default chat agent: form_builder.manager (per-project coordinator clone).
Purpose: form templates (create/manage/version) + object insertion (human or schema-constrained LLM fill) + document ISSUING - immutable snapshots with provenance, per-year issue numbers, and supersedes corrections (quotations, official letters, resumes, periodic reports). Owns NO content data (rosters, ledgers live in Ops); a form is a projection of those records. Project-bound surface: marker `project.formproj`, artifacts under `<project>/forms/<issueNumber>/`, templates/drafts/issues persist as facts in the project FactGraph.
Tool surface: host `form.*` capability (13 verbs incl. save_template / create_document / validate / render / template_schema / capacity - template persistence is fact-backed while a form project is bound) + `form_builder.*` (draft_save/draft_get/draft_list/draft_delete + issue/issue_list/issue_get). Authoring/issuing manual = `studio://knowledge/form_builder_manual/*`.

sources.name: Host manager routing manual
sources.description: User-intent → host action playbook. The manager consults this when deciding whether to answer inline, dispatch to a built-in agent, or call a system tool.

documents.title: Intent → route
documents.content:
INSTALL / LIST / ACTIVATE BUNDLES
  user: 'what bundles do I have' / 'install <path>' / 'open <bundle>'
  action: call `studio.bundle.list` (list) · `studio.bundle.install` (install · internal — see gate) · `studio.bundle.activate` (open new tab) directly. Report the result inline.

OPEN A BUILT-IN APP
  user: 'open App Builder' / 'launch Scene Builder' / 'go to Ops'
  action: `studio.chrome.open_seed` with the built-in id (`app_builder` / `scene_builder` / `makemind_ops`). Then dispatch to that builtin's manager via `bk.agent.dispatch` if the user's request needs in-domain work.

AUTHORING / EDITING A BUNDLE
  user: 'create a counter app' / 'add a settings page'
  action: ensure App Builder tab is open, then `bk.agent.dispatch app_builder.manager` with the user's request as the input. The App Builder manager fans out to ux_designer / ui_implementer / etc.

RECORD A DEMO / TUTORIAL VIDEO
  user: 'record a demo of …'
  action: open Scene Builder, dispatch to `scene_builder.manager`.

WORKSPACE OPERATIONS (members / tasks / processes / knowledge)
  user: 'add a member' / 'create a task' / 'list our skills'
  action: open Ops, dispatch to `ops.manager`.

INTROSPECTION / DEBUG
  user: 'what agents do we have' / 'which tools' / 'debug state'
  action: call `bk.agent.list` · `studio.meta.list_tools` · `studio.debug.config` · `studio.debug.tabs` · `studio.debug.servers` directly and report.

KNOWLEDGE QUERIES
  user: 'how do I …' / 'what does X mean'
  action: `bk.knowledge.query` first (search the seed corpus), then synthesise. Don't guess when the answer requires schema or naming detail — surface the source you cited.

Always prefer calling a tool to inventing an answer; the catalog is rich and `bk.knowledge.query` covers nearly every concept question.

documents.title: Safety rules
documents.content:
1. Never invent agent ids / tool names / bundle paths — call `bk.agent.list` / `studio.meta.list_tools` / `studio.bundle.list` first when uncertain.
2. `studio.chrome.create_package` · `studio.bundle.install` · `studio.bundle.activate` · `studio.bundle.uninstall` are internal — the host gates external callers. Surface the gate's reject message verbatim when you hit one.
3. When dispatching with `bk.agent.dispatch`, pass the user's original intent (or a clear paraphrase) as the `input`; do not over-summarise.
4. Tool errors surface as `[error] …` in this chat — relay them to the user with the corrective action (e.g. 'set the API key in Settings → LLM') instead of pretending the call succeeded.
5. When `bk.knowledge.query` returns no hits, say so and ask the user to clarify or point at a doc — don't extrapolate.

sources.name: Studio debugging & UI-verification manual
sources.description: How an LLM (or the manager) drives, inspects, and VERIFIES the Studio UI over MCP for debugging — the loop that ties the studio.debug.* / studio.renderer.* / studio.ui.* tool references into an end-to-end workflow. Read this before trying to reproduce a UI bug or confirm a fix on screen.

documents.title: The debugging loop + the #1 gotcha
documents.content:
Debugging the Studio UI over MCP is a loop: OPEN the target app -> BIND a project (if the domain needs one) -> INSPECT what is on screen -> DRIVE it (click/type) -> CAPTURE + ASSERT -> iterate. Each step maps to real tools (below).

#1 GOTCHA (this trips everyone, including the people who built it): a built-in app's domain tools register ONLY AFTER that app is open AND its project is bound. Before that, `tools/list` shows just the host surface (`studio.*`) + already-mounted apps (e.g. `app_builder.*`) and NONE of the domain tools you want (`workspace_*`, `member_*`, `ui_*`). Seeing them 'missing' almost always means 'app not open / no project bound' — NOT 'tool does not exist'. So always bootstrap first.

Golden rule: prefer a DOMAIN tool over a synthetic click when one exists (e.g. Ops `workspace_switch {id}` beats tapping the dropdown) — it is faster and deterministic. Use synthetic UI driving for what has no tool, and for confirming the CHROME renders the result.

documents.title: Open an app + bind a project (so its tools appear)
documents.content:
1. OPEN a built-in app: `studio.chrome.open_seed {id}` where id = `app_builder` | `scene_builder` | `makemind_ops`. This mounts the app and registers its tool surface.
2. BIND a project (domains like Ops need one; App Builder/Scene Builder use their own project tools). For Ops in the CURRENT tab: `studio.project.new {name, parent}` (create + bind) or `studio.project.open {path}` (open existing, no dialog). `parent` defaults to settings.workspaceDir; pass an absolute path to control location.
3. CONFIRM: `studio.project.info {}` -> `{packageName, packagePath}`. Only now do `workspace_create` / `workspace_list` / `member_create_agent` / `ui_*` show up in `tools/list`.

SAFETY: never drive the user's live project. Create a throwaway under a scratch dir (`studio.project.new {name:'dbg', parent:'/tmp/...'}`), verify, then delete the folder. This needs no settings edits — project.new binds the current tab directly.

documents.title: See what is on screen (without clicking)
documents.content:
Read the UI before and after every action.

- `studio.renderer.layout_snapshot` -> widget tree + TEXT content. BEST for asserting a label/value is present (e.g. the Home header shows 'Marketing'). It walks the chrome captureRoot AND `WidgetsBinding.rootElement`, so showDialog/overlay content surfaces too. Resolution-independent — prefer it over pixels for text assertions.
- `studio.renderer.current_view` -> the active domain view id.
- `studio.debug.screenshot {pixelRatio?}` or `studio.renderer.screenshot {area?, pixelRatio?}` -> a PNG. Screenshots capture the WHOLE window including open dialogs/overlays (root-navigator), so a dialog you opened is visible in the shot. `area` = `window` | `body` | `left_panel` | `{x,y,w,h}` (logical px). Image is returned as `content[].type=='image'` base64 — decode it to a file to view. Use pixels for layout/spacing/visual bugs where text is not enough.

NATIVE vs DSL: the Ops / App Builder native Flutter chrome is NOT a DSL UI runtime. So `ui_page_state` returns `{attached:false}` and `ui_capture` / `ui_navigate` / `ui_state` target the DSL surface only. Capture the native chrome via `studio.debug.screenshot` / `studio.renderer.*`; use `ui_*` for DSL-rendered views inside an app.

`studio.ui.find {query}` matches tagged (inspectTag) widgets first and falls back to VISIBLE TEXT on any page (matchedField `visibleText`, elementId null) - tap the returned rect centre: `studio.ui.tap {x: rect.x+rect.width/2, y: rect.y+rect.height/2}`. This works on native built-in pages (rail labels, list cards, dialog buttons), so prefer find->tap over guessing coordinates.

documents.title: Interact programmatically (synthetic pointer + keyboard)
documents.content:
`studio.ui.*` drives the app through the Flutter binding (no macOS accessibility, no stealing the user's real pointer/focus). Resolve `elementId` from a `layout_snapshot` rect — accepts a bare `id` or `<type>:<key>`.

- `studio.ui.tap {elementId | x,y, mode?: tap|long|double}` — synthetic click.
- `studio.ui.type {text, elementId?, clear?, submit?}` — sets the focused TextField's controller directly (bypasses IME, so Korean/CJK does not garble); `submit:true` fires onSubmitted (Enter).
- `studio.ui.scroll {elementId|x,y, dx, dy}` · `studio.ui.hover` (tooltip/hover capture) · `studio.ui.right_click` (context menu) · `studio.ui.drag {from, to, steps?}` (splitter / DnD) · `studio.ui.dismiss_dialog` (pop topmost route).
- `studio.ui.set_center_mode {UI|Bundle|Debug}` — 3-way center switch.
- DSL views: `ui_navigate` / `ui_capture`.

Pattern: tap/type to open a menu or fill a field, then re-`layout_snapshot` to confirm the resulting state before the next action.

documents.title: Assert, visual-regress, and diagnose non-visual state
documents.content:
ASSERT-BY-STRUCTURE (preferred): after an action, `layout_snapshot` and check the expected text / elementId is present. Durable across window sizes and themes.

VISUAL REGRESSION: `studio.renderer.image_diff {a, b, threshold?}` -> `{score, diffPixels, totalPixels, w, h}` — both PNGs must share dimensions. `studio.debug.snapshot_diff` diffs layout snapshots. Capture a baseline, drive, capture again, diff, report.

VERIFY THE TRIGGER FIRED: before trusting a before/after differential, confirm the action actually took effect (state changed / a tool returned ok). A silently-failed action (wrong arg name, unbound project) leaves state unchanged and reads as a false 'no change = correct'.

DIAGNOSE non-visual state when the UI looks wrong: `studio.debug.dispatch_log` (recent tool dispatches) · `boot` / `notify` · `tabs` / `activation` / `bundles` / `runtimes` / `runtime_state` · `agents` / `chat` · `config` / `settings` / `overrides` · `workspace_snapshot` (workspaceDir mbds + projects) · `history.{list,diff,restore}` · `wait_for` / `set_state` / `dispatch_tool` · `servers` (DomainServerManager pool).

documents.title: MCP-over-HTTP mechanics (the parsing traps)
documents.content:
Studio serves MCP at `http://localhost:<port>/mcp` (streamable-HTTP; debug 7840, release 7830).

1. POST `initialize` -> reuse the `mcp-session-id` RESPONSE HEADER on every later call. Send `notifications/initialized` once, then `tools/call`.
2. Call a tool with `{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"<tool>","arguments":{...}}}`. Using the tool name AS the JSON-RPC method returns `-32601 Method not found` (a common first-timer mistake).
3. Responses arrive as SSE `data: {json}` frames. Parse each `data:` line with a real JSON parser. Naive text splitting (grep/sed) breaks on the large `tools/list` (~530 tools) and makes tools look absent — this is a frequent false 'tool not found'.
4. Image tools return `content[].type=='image'` base64 (not text) — decode to a PNG file to view; a text-only reader silently drops them.

sources.name: Bundle authoring runbook — three app kinds and authoring flow
sources.description: Procedural guide for authoring manifests: the three app kinds, manifest category checklist, and wiring steps. Advisory tone — cases and procedure, not hard rules. Source: specs/platform/02-bundle-interface.md, 04-ui-host.md.

documents.title: Three app kinds — studio app, server app, bundle app
documents.content:
Studio app (built-in): registered as a BuiltInApp in host code. UI + tools + wiring all wired in code at boot. Seed manifests (studio.mbd, app_builder.mbd, etc.) declare only agents + knowledge — code handles the rest. Suitable for host-level capabilities that ship with the binary.

Server app: a host that runs a KernelApp + bundle and exposes it over MCP (Pattern 1 or Pattern 3). The server serves manifest.json at bundle://manifest.json, UI at ui://, tools at tools/list, knowledge at kb://. Clients reconstruct and run the bundle identically to a local install. Suitable for multi-tenant or remotely-distributed bundles.

Bundle app (.mbd / .mcpb): a self-contained .mbd directory or packed .mcpb archive installed into a host (studio.bundle.install). The host activates it via BundleActivation. Suitable for user-authored apps, marketplace distribution, domain extensions.

Choosing: if the capability is host-core (ships in binary, always on) → studio app (built-in). If the app must be distributed to remote clients as a running service → server app. For everything else — user apps, marketplace, domain knowledge bundles → bundle app.

Reference: specs/platform/00-overview.md, 04-ui-host.md

documents.title: Manifest authoring — category checklist and procedure
documents.content:
Manifest categories and their authoring steps:

1. Identity (manifest.id/name/version/description/type): set first. id must be unique across the host's bundle pool. manifest.type is the kind of app, chosen when the project is created in App Builder, and the bundle is built to it: "application" (the default, AppPlayer App) runs on AppPlayer and in Studio — build its screens and tools from the standard mcp_ui_dsl and portable tools; "extension" (Studio Package) is a Studio app — its screens and composition are built for Studio and may use Studio's widgets (Vbu*), studio.* tools and Studio atoms; "server" (Cloud Server App) is served, not installed. The market shows where an app runs from type.

2. requires.builtinAtoms[]: list the host capability categories the bundle's JS / DSL surface calls (e.g. 'mcp', 'fs', 'ui', 'workspace', 'kb', 'agent', 'bus', 'bundle'). These are coarse host-bridge atoms (host.<atom>.<verb>), NOT mcp_ui_dsl widget atoms. Strict gate — host refuses activation when an entry is not in its advertised set. Leave empty for a fully portable bundle.

3. tools.tools[]: domain logic tools. Each entry needs name (unique within bundle), description, inputSchema, kind ('js' for in-bundle JS), target.entry (path in tools/) and target.fn. Name must NOT start with 'bk.' — those are reserved for knowledge tools. Never put the bundle id in a name: the host adds it when it registers the tool (other bundles and external clients see <id>.<name>). Inside the bundle — screens, JS, wiring, agent allowlists — call the tool by this declared name.

4. agents[]: one entry per agent. Assign id, name, role (manager/worker/reviewer), model, systemPrompt. Add tools allowlist only when narrowing from role default is needed (platform spec 10 — knowledge source spec_platform). The manager agent's systemPrompt should include routing rules and which knowledge sources to query.

5. 4 axis (skills/profiles/philosophies/facts): declare domain knowledge assets. BundleActivation registers them automatically. ids are scoped to the bundle namespace at activation.

6. ui: path to the entry mcp_ui_dsl JSON (e.g. 'ui/app.json'). Omit if the bundle has no UI.

7. wiring: connect chrome slots. lifecycle[] maps standard slot ids (project.new/open/save etc.) to the bundle's declared tool names (or host tools such as studio.*). domainActions[] declares row-2 icon buttons. titlebar/statusbar set text templates. settings[] lists settings entries.

8. settings.sections: declare inline settings fields (type: secret/string/bool/select etc.). Host settings dialog renders these; changes autosave.

9. knowledge.sources: advisory reference documents for LLM agents. Each source has id, name, description, documents[{id, title, content}].

For seed bundles (built-ins): only categories 4 and 9 are typically needed — tools/ui/wiring/settings are wired in code.

Reference: specs/platform/02-bundle-interface.md

documents.title: Wiring authoring — chrome slot connection patterns
documents.content:
wiring.lifecycle connects standard chrome button slots to bundle tool calls:
  { "slot": "project.new", "tool": "myCreateTool" }
Standard slots include: project.new, project.open, project.save, project.close, project.export, edit.undo, edit.redo, history.show, edit.revert. Only declare slots the bundle actually handles.

wiring.domainActions declares row-2 domain icon buttons in chrome. Each entry needs tool (raw name within bundle — host prefixes <bundleId>. automatically), icon, and tooltip.

wiring.titlebar / wiring.statusbar: text with optional state binding {{key}} templates. Key values come from the bundle's runtime state.

wiring.settings: entries shown in the domain settings panel, separate from settings.sections fields.

chat.slashCommands: slash chips in the chat composer. { command: '/refresh', tool: 'refresh' } — host auto-prefixes the tool name with bundleId on invocation.

Reference: specs/platform/02-bundle-interface.md §6

sources.name: UI DSL specification 1.4
sources.description: The published UI DSL specification 1.4 (specs-pub/ui_dsl/1.4/), one document per section. Generated by tool/embed_spec_knowledge.py — do not edit.

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 00. Overview
documents.content: # 00. Overview

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 00. Overview — 0.1 What is MCP UI DSL?
documents.content:
## 0.1 What is MCP UI DSL?

MCP UI DSL is a JSON-based domain-specific language for declarative, reactive user interfaces in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem. A server (or an AI agent) emits a JSON definition; any MCP-capable client renders it without application-specific code.

Three properties are definitional:

1. **Declarative.** The JSON describes *what* the UI is, not *how* to construct it. Runtimes own the rendering strategy.
2. **Server-driven.** The authoritative definition lives on the server. Clients fetch, render, and subscribe to updates; they do not author UI.
3. **Language-neutral.** The DSL names and semantics are independent of Flutter, React, Vue, Python, or any specific implementation. A valid definition renders equivalently on every conformant runtime.

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 00. Overview — 0.2 Why MCP UI DSL?
documents.content:
## 0.2 Why MCP UI DSL?

- **Cross-platform parity without duplication.** One definition serves every client.
- **AI-authored UIs.** LLMs can generate valid JSON from a single-document reference.
- **Live updates via MCP.** Resources, subscriptions, and tools are first-class — the UI reacts to server state without polling logic in the definition.
- **Permissioned client capabilities.** File system, network, system info, channels — all available through explicit permission grants (see [`08_Client_Extensions.md`](08_Client_Extensions.md)).

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 00. Overview — 0.3 Scope of this Specification
documents.content:
## 0.3 Scope of this Specification

This specification defines:

- The shape of an ApplicationDefinition and PageDefinition
- The widget catalog (canonical names, properties, aliases)
- Data binding syntax, expression language, and prefix resolution
- The action system
- The theme system
- The MCP protocol contract used by the DSL
- The security model (sandbox, validation, access control)
- Client-side extensions (actions, permissions, channels)
- The template system
- Advanced widgets (charts, canvas, code editor, etc.)
- Bundle metadata and serving
- Internationalization
- Accessibility
- Responsive layout and event propagation
- Offline behavior and sync
- Animations
- Conformance profiles

This specification does **not** define:

- How a specific runtime implementation is structured internally.
- Which widgets are mapped to which native platform widgets (a Flutter implementation's `text` → Flutter `Text`, a React implementation's → `<span>`; these are implementation choices).
- Any single product's UI design language beyond the theme tokens.

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 00. Overview — 0.4 How to Read This Specification
documents.content:
## 0.4 How to Read This Specification

Start here. Then:

| If you are... | Read... |
|---------------|---------|
| A runtime implementer | [`01_Core_Concepts.md`](01_Core_Concepts.md), [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md), then sections matching your target profiles |
| A UI author (human or AI) | [`02_Widgets.md`](02_Widgets.md), [`03_Data_Binding.md`](03_Data_Binding.md), [`04_Actions.md`](04_Actions.md) |
| A bundle packager | [`11_Bundle_Metadata.md`](11_Bundle_Metadata.md) |
| A client-capability integrator | [`08_Client_Extensions.md`](08_Client_Extensions.md) |
| Seeking a specific name | [`17_Naming.md`](17_Naming.md) |

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 00. Overview — 0.5 Terminology
documents.content:
## 0.5 Terminology

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **Application** | A complete MCP UI app: routes, pages, theme, global state. Defined by an `ApplicationDefinition`. |
| **Page** | A full-screen view within an application. Defined by a `PageDefinition`. Canonical `type` value is `"page"`; `"screen"` is a legacy alias. |
| **Widget** | A UI component declared by a `"type"` field in JSON. The widget catalog is in [`02_Widgets.md`](02_Widgets.md). |
| **Action** | An operation triggered by user interaction or lifecycle events. Types: `state`, `navigation`, `tool`, etc. See [`04_Actions.md`](04_Actions.md). |
| **Binding** | A reactive expression in `{{...}}` syntax. Resolves against state, theme, route params, etc. See [`03_Data_Binding.md`](03_Data_Binding.md). |
| **Template** | A reusable, parameterized widget tree invoked via `"type": "use"`. See [`09_Templates.md`](09_Templates.md). |
| **Channel** | A bidirectional real-time data stream between client and server (Client Profile). See [`08_Client_Extensions.md`](08_Client_Extensions.md). |
| **Bundle** | A packaged MCP application containing UI definitions, assets, and manifest. See [`11_Bundle_Metadata.md`](11_Bundle_Metadata.md). |
| **Runtime** | The client-side implementation that parses a definition and renders widgets. |
| **Generator** | A library (or AI agent) that produces DSL JSON. |
| **Profile** | A named subset of DSL capabilities used for conformance declarations. See [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md). |
| **Canonical name** | The preferred identifier for a concept. Emitters MUST use canonical names. |
| **Legacy alias** | An accepted alternative name for a canonical identifier. Accepted on input; never emitted. Registered in [`17_Naming.md`](17_Naming.md). |

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 00. Overview — 0.6 Requirement Levels
documents.content:
## 0.6 Requirement Levels

This specification uses **MUST / SHOULD / MAY** per RFC 2119 / RFC 8174:

- **MUST** — absolute requirement. A non-conformant runtime fails.
- **SHOULD** — strong recommendation. A runtime MAY diverge with documented reason.
- **MAY** — optional. Either behavior is conformant.

Requirements are anchored in [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md) per profile. Other sections describe behavior and reference the conformance file for normative binding.

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 00. Overview — 0.7 Versioning and `since:` Markers
documents.content:
## 0.7 Versioning and `since:` Markers

Features introduced after v1.0 carry a `since: vX.Y` marker in their heading or schema table. The marker is informational — it tells implementers which MCP UI DSL version first introduced the feature.

Implementations declare support via **Profiles** (see [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md)), not via version numbers. A runtime may implement all of v1.0 but only the Core Profile parts of v1.1.

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 00. Overview — 0.8 JSON Conventions
documents.content:
## 0.8 JSON Conventions

- **Key style:** camelCase.
- **Enum value style:** lowercase single-word or camelCase multi-word.
- **Comments:** JSON does not support comments; inline `//` comments in this document's examples are informative only and MUST be removed from any actual JSON sent across the wire.
- **Required fields** are marked `required: true` in schema tables. Absence MUST produce a parse error.
- **Optional fields** with defaults show the default value in the schema table.

See [`17_Naming.md`](17_Naming.md) §17.1 for the complete naming conventions.

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 01. Core Concepts
documents.content:
# 01. Core Concepts

This document defines the three definition types that form every MCP UI DSL program, the scopes under which state lives, the lifecycle hooks that bound that state, and the version field that gates features.

Full canonical-name and legacy-alias references live in [`17_Naming.md`](17_Naming.md). Normative requirements (MUST / SHOULD / MAY) are anchored in [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md).

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 01. Core Concepts — 1.1 The Definition Tree
documents.content:
## 1.1 The Definition Tree

Every program the runtime consumes is one of three definition shapes:

| Definition | `type` value | Role |
|------------|--------------|------|
| **ApplicationDefinition** | `"application"` | Top-level container — owns routes, theme, app-wide state, navigation chrome |
| **PageDefinition** | `"page"` | Full-screen view referenced by a route |
| **WidgetDefinition** | widget type string (e.g. `"box"`, `"text"`) | UI node within a page's content tree |

The program forms a tree:

```
ApplicationDefinition
 ├── theme, navigation, state (app scope), lifecycle (app hooks), services
 └── routes: { "/path": DefinitionSource }
              └── PageDefinition
                   ├── state (page scope), lifecycle (page hooks)
                   └── content: WidgetDefinition
                                 └── child | children: WidgetDefinition[...]
```

Page trees are resolved lazily: a route value may be an inline `PageDefinition` or a URI (`"ui://pages/dashboard"`) that the runtime reads via the MCP resource protocol. See [`06_Runtime_Contract.md`](06_Runtime_Contract.md) §6.1 for the resolution contract.

Since v1.4 a definition may also be sourced from an **origin other than the one serving the document** — see §1.9 `DefinitionSource`. That is what lets one application compose several MCP servers.

### 1.1.1 Canonical vs Legacy Root Types

The root `type` for a page definition is canonically `"page"`. The legacy value `"screen"` is accepted by conformant runtimes (see [`17_Naming.md`](17_Naming.md) §17.3.5). Emitters MUST emit `"page"`.

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 01. Core Concepts — 1.2 ApplicationDefinition
documents.content:
## 1.2 ApplicationDefinition

An ApplicationDefinition is the entry point. The runtime loads it first and derives all other rendering from its routes, theme, and state.

### 1.2.1 Schema

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|:--------:|:-----:|-------------|
| `type` | string (`"application"`) | yes | v1.0 | Discriminator. |
| `routes` | `{ [path: string]: RouteValue }` | yes | v1.0 | Map of route path to a `RouteValue`: any [`DefinitionSource`](#19-definitionsource-since-v14) (inline `PageDefinition`, a `ui://` URI string, a qualified `{ $ref, from }` reference *(since v1.4)*, or a binding expression *(since v1.4)*), or a `{ page, transition }` wrapper that attaches a per-route `RouteTransition` (since v1.3). Path syntax supports parameters: `"/users/:id"`. |
| `title` | string | no | v1.0 | Human-readable name shown by hosts and app launchers. |
| `version` | string | no | v1.0 | DSL version the definition targets. Defaults to `"1.0"`. See §1.7. |
| `initialRoute` | string | no | v1.0 | Route entered at launch. If omitted the runtime picks the first route in declaration order. |
| `theme` | ThemeDefinition | no | v1.0 | Application-wide theme. See [`05_Theme.md`](05_Theme.md). |
| `navigation` | NavigationConfig | no | v1.0 | Global navigation chrome (drawer, bottom bar, rail, tabs). |
| `state` | `{ "initial": object }` | no | v1.0 | Initial application-scope state. Accessible via `{{app.*}}`. See §1.6. |
| `lifecycle` | LifecycleHooks | no | v1.0 | Application-lifetime hooks (see §1.5). |
| `services` | `{ [name: string]: ServiceDefinition }` | no | v1.0 | Background services (polling, subscriptions) launched at app init. |
| `id` | string | no | v1.2 | Stable bundle identifier (reverse-DNS, e.g. `"com.example.myapp"`). See [`11_Bundle_Metadata.md`](11_Bundle_Metadata.md) §11.1. |
| `description` | string | no | v1.2 | Short human-readable description. See [`11_Bundle_Metadata.md`](11_Bundle_Metadata.md) §11.1. |
| `icon` | IconReference | no | v1.2 | App icon reference. See [`11_Bundle_Metadata.md`](11_Bundle_Metadata.md) §11.1. |
| `splash` | SplashConfig | no | v1.2 | Splash-screen configuration. See [`11_Bundle_Metadata.md`](11_Bundle_Metadata.md) §11.4. |
| `category` | string | no | v1.2 | Classification tag (e.g. `"productivity"`, `"utility"`). |
| `publisher` | PublisherInfo | no | v1.2 | Publisher metadata. See [`11_Bundle_Metadata.md`](11_Bundle_Metadata.md) §11.2. |
| `timestamps` | TimestampInfo | no | v1.2 | Creation / update timestamps. See [`11_Bundle_Metadata.md`](11_Bundle_Metadata.md) §11.3. |
| `screenshots` | string[] | no | v1.2 | Reference URIs for store/listing screenshots. |
| `dashboard` | DashboardDefinition | no | v1.3 | Compact rendering entry point. See [`11_Bundle_Metadata.md`](11_Bundle_Metadata.md) §11.9. |
| `templates` | `{ [name: string]: TemplateDefinition }` | no | v1.3 | Application-scope reusable templates. See [`09_Templates.md`](09_Templates.md) §9.2. |
| `templateLibraries` | TemplateLibraryRef[] | no | v1.3 | References to external template collections. See [`09_Templates.md`](09_Templates.md) §9.9. |
| `i18n` | I18nConfig | no | v1.3 | Locale bundles and default locale. See [`12_Internationalization.md`](12_Internationalization.md). |

### 1.2.2 Example

```json
{
  "type": "application",
  "version": "1.3",
  "id": "com.example.taskflow",
  "title": "TaskFlow",
  "description": "A lightweight task tracker.",
  "initialRoute": "/dashboard",
  "theme": {
    "mode": "system",
    "colors": { "primary": "#2196F3", "surface": "#F5F5F5" }
  },
  "routes": {
    "/dashboard": "ui://pages/dashboard",
    "/tasks/:id": "ui://pages/task-detail"
  },
  "state": {
    "initial": {
      "user": { "name": "Guest", "isAuthenticated": false },
      "filter": "all"
    }
  },
  "lifecycle": {
    "onInit": { "type": "tool", "tool": "loadSession" },
    "onDestroy": { "type": "tool", "tool": "persistSession" }
  },
  "navigation": {
    "type": "drawer",
    "items": [
      { "label": "Dashboard", "route": "/dashboard", "icon": "dashboard" }
    ]
  }
}
```

### 1.2.3 NavigationConfig

The `navigation` field on ApplicationDefinition declares the global navigation chrome.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|:--------:|:-----:|-------------|
| `type` | enum (`drawer` / `bottomBar` / `rail` / `tabs`) | yes | v1.0 | Chrome style. `drawer` = side drawer; `bottomBar` = bottom navigation; `rail` = vertical rail; `tabs` = tab strip. |
| `items` | NavItem[] | no | v1.0 | Navigation entries. Each entry: `{ label, icon?, activeIcon?, route, badge?, children?, onTap?, style? }` — `activeIcon` is shown in place of `icon` while that entry is selected. |
| `header` | Widget | no | v1.0 | Optional header widget rendered above `items` (used by `drawer` / `rail`). |
| `footer` | Widget | no | v1.0 | Optional footer widget rendered below `items` (used by `drawer` / `rail`). |
| `style` | `NavigationStyle` | no | v1.3 | Visual styling for the navigation surface (backgroundColor / backgroundImage / indicatorColor / indicatorShape / `dividerColor` / `dividerThickness` / `dividerIndent` / labelStyle / iconStyle / selectedColor / unselectedColor / elevation). Per-item overrides via `NavItem.style`. |

```json
{
  "navigation": {
    "type": "drawer",
    "items": [
      { "label": "Home", "route": "/", "icon": "home" },
      { "label": "Settings", "route": "/settings", "icon": "settings" }
    ],
    "header": { "type": "text", "text": "Acme Corp" },
    "footer": { "type": "button", "label": "Sign out", "onTap": { "type": "tool", "tool": "signOut" } }
  }
}
```

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 01. Core Concepts — 1.3 PageDefinition
UI DSL 1.4 · 01. Core Concepts — 1.4 WidgetDefinition
documents.content:
## 1.4 WidgetDefinition

A WidgetDefinition is any JSON object with a `type` field that names a widget from the catalog in [`02_Widgets.md`](02_Widgets.md).

### 1.4.1 Common Shape

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `type` | string | Widget type name. Required. |
| `child` | WidgetDefinition | Sole child (single-child widgets). |
| `children` | WidgetDefinition[] | Children list (multi-child widgets). Single-child widgets accept a one-element `children` array for authoring convenience. |
| `visible` | boolean | Default `true`. When `false` the subtree is not rendered. |
| `tooltip` | string | Hover / long-press tooltip wrapper. See [`02_Widgets.md`](02_Widgets.md) §2.2. |
| `click` | Action | Tap action fired by a gesture-surface wrap. See [`02_Widgets.md`](02_Widgets.md) §2.2 and [`04_Actions.md`](04_Actions.md). |
| `accessibility` | AccessibilityBlock | Grouped a11y fields (`label`, `hint`, `role`, `live`, ...). See [`13_Accessibility.md`](13_Accessibility.md). |
| `style`, `padding`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, ... | widget-specific | Per-widget properties. See [`02_Widgets.md`](02_Widgets.md). |
| `id` | string | Optional stable handle for test hooks and action targeting. |

All widget-specific properties (e.g. `src` on `image`, `label` on `button`, `text` on `text`) are collected in the same JSON object alongside `type`. There is no separate property bag.

### 1.4.2 Composition Rules

- Single-child widgets (`box`, `center`, `padding`, `card`, ...) expect `child`.
- Multi-child widgets (`linear`, `stack`, `wrap`, `list`, `grid`, ...) expect `children` (an array).
- When a single-child widget receives `children` with exactly one element, the runtime treats it as equivalent to `child`.
- When both `child` and `children` are provided, `child` wins and the runtime MAY emit a warning.

### 1.4.3 Example

```json
{
  "type": "box",
  "padding": { "all": 16 },
  "decoration": { "color": "{{theme.colors.surface}}", "borderRadius": 8 },
  "child": {
    "type": "linear",
    "direction": "vertical",
    "spacing": 8,
    "children": [
      { "type": "text", "text": "{{page.title}}", "style": { "fontWeight": "bold" } },
      { "type": "button", "label": "Continue", "onTap": { "type": "navigation", "action": "push", "route": "/next" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 01. Core Concepts — 1.5 Lifecycle Hooks
documents.content:
## 1.5 Lifecycle Hooks

Lifecycle hooks bind actions to well-defined moments in the lifetime of an Application, a Page, or a template instance.

### 1.5.1 Hook Names

| Hook | Fires |
|------|-------|
| `onInit` | Immediately after the definition is parsed and state is initialized; before any render. |
| `onReady` | After the first successful render / mount. Safe to call tools that depend on bound state. |
| `onMount` | When the definition becomes part of the live tree (page shown, template instance inserted). |
| `onPause` | When the definition loses active focus but is not destroyed (e.g. navigated away from on a stack). |
| `onResume` | When a paused definition regains active focus. |
| `onUnmount` | When the definition is removed from the live tree. |
| `onDestroy` | When the runtime releases the definition; state is disposed after this hook returns. |

Each hook value is a single Action or an Action array. Arrays execute sequentially. See [`04_Actions.md`](04_Actions.md).

### 1.5.2 Firing Order

For a given definition instance:

```
onInit → onMount → onReady → (onPause ↔ onResume)* → onUnmount → onDestroy
```

`onReady` always fires after `onMount`. Paused instances may cycle `onPause`/`onResume` any number of times before unmount. Runtimes MUST guarantee `onUnmount` runs even when removal is caused by conditional rendering. See [`06_Runtime_Contract.md`](06_Runtime_Contract.md) §6.8 for the normative contract.

**"A given definition instance" is the whole of it.** Navigating away from a page destroys that page's instance; navigating back builds a new one, and a new instance starts at `onInit` again. Returning to a page is therefore *not* a resume — an author who fetches in a page's `onInit` is writing "fetch every time this page is opened", which is a reasonable thing to want and an expensive surprise when it was not.

`onPause`/`onResume` cover the other case: an instance that is kept alive while it loses focus. Two navigations do keep it — a stack that pushes over a page keeps the one underneath, and a shell that switches between pages (tab bar, rail, bottom bar) keeps every page already visited. A navigation that *replaces* a page does not, so a document MUST NOT assume either. Work that should happen once per *document* belongs in the application's `onInit`/`onReady`, which run once for the application instance no matter how many times its pages are opened.

### 1.5.3 Placement: Definition-Level vs Instance-Level

Lifecycle hooks appear in two distinct positions, and the placement is not interchangeable:

**Definition-level (top-level fields on the definition object).** Applies to ApplicationDefinition, PageDefinition, and TemplateDefinition. The hook names appear as sibling fields alongside `type`, `content`, `state`, etc. These run for the definition as a whole.

```json
{
  "type": "page",
  "onInit": { "type": "tool", "tool": "loadData" },
  "onReady": { "type": "state", "action": "set", "binding": "page.ready", "value": true },
  "onDestroy": { "type": "tool", "tool": "flushCache" },
  "content": { "type": "box", "child": { "type": "text", "text": "Hello" } }
}
```

Equivalently (and preferred for a large set of hooks), a definition-level `lifecycle` object may group them:

```json
{
  "type": "page",
  "lifecycle": {
    "onInit": { "type": "tool", "tool": "loadData" },
    "onReady": { "type": "state", "action": "set", "binding": "page.ready", "value": true },
    "onDestroy": { "type": "tool", "tool": "flushCache" }
  },
  "content": { "type": "box", "child": { "type": "text", "text": "Hello" } }
}
```

When both top-level hook fields and a `lifecycle` object are present on the same definition, the two sets are merged; a name appearing in both positions is an error and the runtime MUST reject the definition.

**Instance-level (on a template invocation).** A `use` widget that invokes a template may declare instance-specific hooks. Instance hooks are always wrapped in a `lifecycle:` block — never placed as top-level fields on the `use` widget:

```json
{
  "type": "use",
  "template": "expandablePanel",
  "params": { "title": "Advanced" },
  "lifecycle": {
    "onMount": { "type": "tool", "tool": "trackImpression", "params": { "component": "advanced-panel" } },
    "onUnmount": { "type": "tool", "tool": "flushMetrics" }
  }
}
```

Instance hooks run for that particular template instance only and see the instance's `local.*` scope. They do not replace the template definition's own hooks — both fire, with the definition's hook first.

### 1.5.4 Hook Errors

If a hook action fails, the runtime logs the error and continues. It MUST NOT cancel the remaining lifecycle sequence. `onError` callbacks declared on individual actions (see [`04_Actions.md`](04_Actions.md) §4.7) remain the correct recovery mechanism.

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 01. Core Concepts — 1.6 State Scopes
documents.content:
## 1.6 State Scopes

State in MCP UI DSL is partitioned into four scopes. Each scope has a distinct lifetime and a distinct binding prefix. The resolution order for unprefixed identifiers is specified in [`03_Data_Binding.md`](03_Data_Binding.md) §3.4.

| Scope | Prefix | Lifetime | Mutability | Declared in |
|-------|--------|----------|------------|-------------|
| Application | `app.*` | From application load until `onDestroy` | Read-write via `state` actions | ApplicationDefinition `state.initial` |
| Page | `page.*` | From page mount until unmount | Read-write via `state` actions | PageDefinition `state.initial` |
| Local (template instance) | `local.*` | From template instance mount until unmount | Read-write via `state` actions | TemplateDefinition `stateDefaults` *(since v1.3)* |
| Route parameters | `route.params.*` | The current route's active lifetime | Read-only | Route path segments (`/users/:id` → `route.params.id`) |

### 1.6.1 Isolation

- Sibling pages do not share `page.*` state; unmounting a page disposes its state.
- Sibling template instances do not share `local.*` state; each `use` gets its own copy of `stateDefaults`. See [`09_Templates.md`](09_Templates.md) §9.7.
- `app.*` state persists across page transitions and is the only scope suitable for cross-page communication.

### 1.6.2 Read-only Scopes

`route.params.*` is read-only. Any `state` action targeting `route.params.*` MUST be rejected by the runtime. To change route parameters, emit a `navigation` action that pushes or replaces the route with new parameter values (see [`04_Actions.md`](04_Actions.md) §4.2).

Additional read-only binding prefixes (`theme.*`, `client.*`, `permissions.*`, `channels.*`, `resources.*`, `sync.*`, `runtime.*`, `i18n.*`, `event.*`) are not state scopes — they expose runtime and context data. The full prefix table is in [`17_Naming.md`](17_Naming.md) §17.2.5.

### 1.6.3 State Actions

State is mutated only through `state` actions:

```json
{ "type": "state", "action": "set", "binding": "app.filter", "value": "active" }
```

Supported sub-actions: `set`, `increment`, `decrement`, `toggle`, `append`, `remove`, `push`, `pop`, `removeAt`. See [`04_Actions.md`](04_Actions.md) §4.2 and [`17_Naming.md`](17_Naming.md) §17.2.4.

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 01. Core Concepts — 1.7 Version Field
documents.content:
## 1.7 Version Field

The `version` field on ApplicationDefinition declares which DSL version the definition targets.

### 1.7.1 Shape

```json
{ "type": "application", "version": "1.3", ... }
```

Accepted string forms: `"1.0"`, `"1.1"`, `"1.2"`, `"1.3"`, `"1.4"`. A three-part form (`"1.4.0"`) is also accepted; comparison uses `major.minor` only. If `version` is omitted the runtime MUST treat the definition as `"1.0"`.

### 1.7.2 Effect on Parsing

A runtime MAY use `version` to decide whether to accept version-gated fields (e.g. `dashboard` on v1.3, `templates` on v1.3, `permissions` on v1.1). Fields newer than the declared version SHOULD be accepted if the runtime supports them (forward-compatibility) but the runtime MAY warn.

**Exception — multi-origin composition (v1.4).** Forward-compatible acceptance does NOT apply to a `DefinitionSource` carrying a `from` origin (§1.9), nor to the [`view`](02_Widgets.md#2131-view-since-v14) widget. A runtime that does not implement the Composition Profile MUST reject those rather than accept them, because a naive reading — resolving `$ref` against the only origin it has — would render *a different server's UI in place of the requested one*. That is a security failure, not a missing feature. See [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md) §18.7.

### 1.7.3 Relationship to Profiles

The `version` field is informational for feature introduction. It is **not** the conformance dimension. A runtime's support surface is declared in terms of Profiles (Core, Client, Bundle, Advanced, Template, Composition, Payment), defined in [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md). A document carrying `version: "1.3"` may be served to a runtime that claims Core Profile only; the runtime accepts the parts inside its profile and rejects or ignores the rest per its documented policy.

### 1.7.4 `since:` Markers

Features introduced after v1.0 carry a `since: vX.Y` marker on their heading or schema row throughout this specification. The marker tells implementers which DSL version first introduced the feature, independently of which profile governs it.

### 1.7.5 Backward Compatibility *(since v1.4.1)*

§1.7.2 governs the forward direction — a document that names an older version may still carry newer fields. This section governs the other one, which costs more when it is wrong.

**A published document MUST keep opening.** Within a major version, the set of values a slot accepts MAY grow and MUST NOT shrink. A validator MUST NOT reject a value that was legal in the version the document declares.

This is not a style preference. **A runtime validates a document at load, not at authoring time** (§18.2.6), so a slot that stops accepting a spelling does not merely refuse a new author — it stops every already-distributed bundle carrying that spelling from opening at all. A bundle in a marketplace is not re-authored when this specification changes; it is a fixed artifact that must still run. "Tightened the schema" and "broke the installed base" are the same event described from two ends.

Consequently:

- **Retiring a spelling is a documentation change, not a validation change.** Remove it from the canonical surface — the prose, the examples, the emitters, the authoring tools — so new documents are written the new way. The validator keeps accepting the old spelling, and the runtime keeps rendering it. §17.3 already describes this arrangement for aliases; §1.7.5 makes it the general rule.
- **Where a slot must genuinely become stricter, gate the strictness on `version`.** The declared version says which contract the document was written against, and that contract is what it is judged by. A document declaring `1.0` is judged by 1.0's rules even on a runtime that implements a later version.
- **A value that resolves to nothing is reported, not rejected.** When a document carries something the runtime cannot make sense of — a spacing token no theme declares, an asset scheme it does not implement — the answer is a diagnostic and the slot's declared fallback, never a refusal to open the document. §6.12.4 says this for assets; it generalizes.
- **Implementation cost is not a reason to break a bundle.** Accepting two spellings is untidy in a way that is confined to one file. A bundle that no longer opens is a failure the author cannot see, cannot reproduce from the document, and cannot fix without republishing.

A narrowing that cannot be expressed any of these ways requires a **major version**, where the break is declared rather than discovered.

Specifically:

- ApplicationDefinition parsing and MCP protocol read: [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md) §18.2.6
- Widget rendering and tree composition: [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md) §18.2.1
- Lifecycle execution order: [`06_Runtime_Contract.md`](06_Runtime_Contract.md) §6.8 (normative behavior) anchored by [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md) §18.2.6
- State isolation across scopes: [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md) §18.2.8 (security §7.4)
- Legacy alias acceptance for `screen`/`page`, `container`/`box`, `content`/`text`, etc.: [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md) §18.2.10 referencing [`17_Naming.md`](17_Naming.md) §17.3

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 01. Core Concepts — 1.9 DefinitionSource *(since v1.4)*
documents.content:
## 1.9 DefinitionSource *(since v1.4)*

A **DefinitionSource** is *where a definition comes from*. Before v1.4 the answer was always "inline, or a `ui://` resource on the one server this runtime is talking to". v1.4 names the concept and lets it point elsewhere, so one application can compose definitions served by several origins.

### 1.9.1 Forms

| Form | Shape | Resolves to | Since |
|------|-------|-------------|:-----:|
| Inline | `PageDefinition` \| `WidgetDefinition` | itself | v1.0 |
| Local URI | `"ui://pages/main"` | resource read from the **current origin** | v1.0 |
| Qualified reference | `{ "$ref": <uri>, "from": Origin }` | resource read from the named origin | v1.4 |
| Binding | `"{{state.path}}"` | a definition already held in state | v1.4 |

A bare string is a local URI when it matches a resource-URI scheme, and a binding when it matches the binding pattern `^\{\{.*\}\}$` (see [`03_Data_Binding.md`](03_Data_Binding.md)). The two are unambiguous.

Omitting `from` means the current origin. **Every v1.3 document therefore keeps its exact meaning under v1.4.**

### 1.9.2 Origin

An `Origin` names *who serves* a definition. It is deliberately open so future sources need no new syntax:

| Shape | Meaning | Since |
|-------|---------|:-----:|
| `{ "connection": <id> }` | A connection in the host's outbound MCP client registry, addressed by the id used to open it. | v1.4 |

The `connection` id is the same identifier the host's `mcp.connect` surface returns — the DSL does not define how connections are made, only how a definition is addressed once one exists. Establishing connections is a host capability, not a DSL feature; see [`06_Runtime_Contract.md`](06_Runtime_Contract.md) §6.11.

`connection` MAY be a binding (`{ "connection": "{{conn.temp}}" }`), which is the normal case: an application opens its connections in `lifecycle.onInit` and stores the ids in state.

Runtimes MUST reject an `Origin` whose sole key they do not recognise, rather than silently falling back to the current origin. Silent fallback would render *the wrong server's UI* — a correctness and security failure, not a cosmetic one.

### 1.9.3 Why the binding form matters

A host's MCP client surface already returns resource contents as data. Reading a definition into state and binding to it therefore requires **no new connection machinery at all**, and the same form covers definitions that never came from a server: agent-generated UI, cached UI, UI loaded from a bundle asset, UI composed at runtime. `DefinitionSource` is general on purpose — "render a definition from elsewhere" is the primitive, and "elsewhere is another MCP server" is one case of it.

### 1.9.4 Where a DefinitionSource is accepted

Exactly two places. One concept, two surfaces:

| Surface | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| `ApplicationDefinition.routes[*]` (§1.2.1) | A whole route is another origin's page. |
| The [`view`](02_Widgets.md#2131-view-since-v14) widget *(since v1.4)* | A definition is embedded anywhere in a widget tree. |

### 1.9.5 Origin is a scope, not an argument

**When a definition is resolved from an origin, that origin becomes the ambient origin for the resolved subtree.** Actions inside it — `tool` calls, `resource` reads and subscriptions — dispatch to that origin. State, storage, and permissions are scoped to it (see [`07_Security.md`](07_Security.md) §7.10 and [`08_Client_Extensions.md`](08_Client_Extensions.md) §8.8).

This is normative and load-bearing. It is what lets a definition authored with no knowledge of any embedder — a device serving its own `ui://app`, saying plainly `{"type": "tool", "tool": "led.set"}` — render **unmodified** inside another application and still reach its own server.

The rejected alternative was a per-action origin field. It would require rewriting every embedded definition, and would make it impossible to embed a server you do not control. An action MAY carry an explicit `origin` to cross scopes deliberately; that is a separate permission and is denied by default (§8.8).

### 1.9.6 Example

```json
{
  "type": "application",
  "version": "1.4",
  "routes": {
    "/":      "ui://pages/main",
    "/temp":  { "$ref": "ui://app", "from": { "connection": "{{conn.temp}}" } },
    "/ctrl":  { "$ref": "ui://views/summary", "from": { "connection": "{{conn.ctrl}}" } }
  },
  "navigation": {
    "type": "bottomBar",
    "items": [
      { "label": "Home", "route": "/", "icon": "home" },
      { "label": "Temp", "route": "/temp", "icon": "thermostat" },
      { "label": "Ctrl", "route": "/ctrl", "icon": "tune" }
    ]
  }
}
```

The route form composes with everything `routes` already supports — `initialRoute` to show an origin's page at launch, a `navigation` action to reveal it on tap, `navigation.items` to put it in the app's chrome. No new navigation concept is introduced.

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 02. Widgets
documents.content:
# 02. Widgets

**Status:** Normative.

> **SSOT:** The machine-readable widget registry at [`widgets/<category>/<type>.yaml`](widgets/) is authoritative. If YAML and prose disagree, YAML wins.
>
> The tables in this file are **curated, not generated** — they carry the canonical properties with the explanation an author needs, and they do not list every declared property. The complete per-widget list, including properties promoted from a runtime that had been reading them undeclared, is [`generated/widgets.md`](generated/widgets.md); the machine form is [`schema/widgets.schema.json`](schema/widgets.schema.json). A property absent from a prose table but present in the registry is still declared and still validated.

This section defines every widget in the Core Profile. The full canonical name list is also summarized in [`17_Naming.md`](17_Naming.md) §17.2.1; all aliases are registered in §17.3. Required widget sets are anchored in [`18_Conformance.md`](18_Conformance.md) §18.2.1. Advanced widgets are defined in [`10_Advanced_Widgets.md`](10_Advanced_Widgets.md).

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 02. Widgets — 2.1 Widget Categories
documents.content:
## 2.1 Widget Categories

- **Layout:** `box`, `linear`, `stack`, `center`, `align`, `padding`, `margin`, `expanded`, `flexible`, `spacer`, `wrap`, `positioned`, `safeArea`, `sizedBox`, `aspectRatio`, `constrained`, `fractionallySized`, `intrinsicHeight`, `intrinsicWidth`, `visibility`, `conditional`, `indexedStack`
- **Display:** `text`, `richText`, `image`, `icon`, `card`, `divider`, `verticalDivider`, `badge`, `chip`, `avatar`, `tooltip`, `placeholder`, `banner`, `progressBar`, `decoration`
- **Input:** `button`, `iconButton`, `textInput`, `toggle`, `select`, `checkbox`, `checkboxGroup`, `radio`, `radioGroup`, `slider`, `rangeSlider`, `numberField`, `dateField`, `timeField`, `datePicker`, `timePicker`, `dateRangePicker`, `colorPicker`, `segmentedControl`, `stepper`, `numberStepper`, `rating`, `form`
- **List:** `list`, `grid`, `listItem`
- **Navigation:** `headerBar`, `bottomNavigation`, `tabBar`, `tabBarView`, `drawer`, `navigationRail`, `floatingActionButton`, `popupMenuButton`
- **Scroll:** `scrollView`, `singleChildScrollView`, `scrollBar`, `pageView`
- **Interaction:** `gestureDetector`, `inkWell`, `draggable`, `dragTarget`
- **Dialog:** `alertDialog`, `simpleDialog`, `customDialog`, `snackBar`, `bottomSheet`
- **Animation:** `animatedContainer`, `opacity` *(since v1.3)*, `transform` *(since v1.3)*, `lottieAnimation`
- **Advanced:** see [`10_Advanced_Widgets.md`](10_Advanced_Widgets.md)
- **Template:** `use`, `template` — see [`09_Templates.md`](09_Templates.md)
- **Accessibility:** `accessibleWrapper` — see [`13_Accessibility.md`](13_Accessibility.md)
- **Utility:** `lazy`, `fittedBox`, `clipOval`, `clipRRect`

documents.title: UI DSL 1.4 · 02. Widgets — 2.2 Common Properties
documents.content:
